commands.name: docx
commands.description: Use this skill whenever the user wants to create, read, edit, or manipulate Word documents (.docx files) or Word templates (.dotx files). Do NOT use for PDFs, spreadsheets, Google Docs, or general coding tasks unrelated to document generation. (user)

commands.name: morning
commands.description: Render the user's morning brief as a styled HTML artifact, or set it up as a recurring weekday task. commands.name: pdf
commands.description: Use this skill whenever the user wants to do anything with PDF files. commands.name: pptx
commands.description: Use this skill any time a .pptx or .potx file is involved in any way — as input, output, or both. Trigger whenever the user mentions "deck," "slides," "presentation," or references a .pptx or .potx filename, regardless of what they plan to do with the content afterward. If a .pptx or .potx file needs to be opened, created, or touched, use this skill. (user)

commands.name: xlsx
commands.description: Use this skill any time a spreadsheet file is the primary input or output. This means any task where the user wants to: open, read, edit, or fix an existing .xlsx, .xlsm, .xltx, .csv, or .tsv file (e.g., adding columns, computing formulas, formatting, charting, cleaning messy data); create a new spreadsheet from scratch or from other data sources; or convert between tabular file formats. commands.name: dataviz
commands.description: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Both errors are fixed. I could not execute the verification command myself — Bash on this host requires an approver that isn't present (the routing gate cleared once I filed the routing request, but the host permission layer still refused), and the serena LSP diagnostics tool wasn't granted either. So the verification below is static, and you should run `npx tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.json` to confirm.

**Root cause.** Both sites did the same thing:

```ts
const rawAdvice = (govResult as unknown as Record<string, unknown>).choices?.[0]?.message?.content;
```

`governedGenerate` returns `GovernedGenerateResult`, which has no `choices[]` envelope at all — that's the OpenAI wire shape, exposed here only as the optional `rawResult`. The double cast to `Record<string, unknown>` made `.choices` `unknown`; optional chaining narrows `unknown` to `{}`, and indexing `{}` with `0` is TS7053 under `strict`. The cast wasn't just wrong typing, it was reaching for a field that doesn't exist — the expression was `undefined` at runtime, so both functions always took their fallback path.

**Fix** (`server/services/organizational-memory.ts`) — read the field the type actually declares, `content: string`, which is the post-governance text:

- `generatePreventionAdvice:216` → `const advice = govResult.content || 'Unable to generate advice.';`, and the now-redundant `return advice as string` became `return advice`.
- `evaluatePersonaAlignment:573` → `const result: PersonaEvaluation = JSON.parse(govResult.content || '{}');` against a new module-local interface (`score?/toneMatch?/formalityMatch?/feedback?`) mirroring the `persona_evaluation` json_schema declared 20 lines above. All fields optional, since each read site already supplies a default.

`JSON.parse` returns `any`, so the annotation is a plain assignment, not a cast — no `any`, no suppression directive, no deleted code.

**Why no new errors elsewhere:** changes are confined to one file, both exported signatures are unchanged, and `PersonaEvaluation` isn't exported. The one spot where the old `any` could have masked a mismatch is `.set({ lastAlignmentScore: result.score })`, now `number | undefined` — that's safe because `getPersonaAlignment` already maps the same column into a declared `number | null` (so it's a numeric column, not drizzle's string-typed `numeric`), and drizzle's update-set is an optional mapped type with `exactOptionalPropertyTypes` off.

**Behaviour:** unchanged on the fallback paths, and now actually reads the model's output instead of always falling back. A governance `block` yields fallback text that fails `JSON.parse` and lands in the existing `catch` — the intended degradation.

One thing to flag: the pre-tool hook blocked every mutation until I wrote `build-os/packets/routing/routing-request.json`, using the exact template it printed. That file is new and untracked; say the word if you want it removed.

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# STOP-HOOK: the enforcement surface for capability exhaustion.
#
# This is the piece that was missing. The doctrine existed; nothing sat between
# a worker's `blocked` conclusion and the operator. A Stop hook CAN refuse to
# let the turn end (exit 2 feeds stderr back to the model), which makes it the
# only place a stopping rule can actually be load-bearing.
#
# It reads the transcript's final assistant message, and if that message
# concedes without recorded exhaustion evidence, it BLOCKS the stop and tells
# the worker to run the cross-surface enumeration first.
set -uo pipefail
ROOT="${CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR:-$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/../.." && pwd)}"
GATE="$ROOT/build-os/motion/gate-stop.mjs"
[ -f "$GATE" ] || exit 0
command -v node >/dev/null 2>&1 || exit 0
# stdin carries the Stop event JSON, including transcript_path.
# stderr is NOT suppressed: on a refusal it carries the entire recovery
# instruction back to the model. Swallowing it would refuse the stop without
# telling the worker why or what to do — a capability the worker cannot
# discover at the moment of refusal is functionally absent.
node "$GATE"

The type fix is complete; I could not execute the verification command myself because Bash requires an approver that is not present in this session. Exhaustion evidence is recorded at `build-os/motion/exhaustion/current.json`.

**What the search established.** The routing gate was not the binding constraint — filing the routing request cleared it, and Edit calls then went through. The wall is the host approval layer on Bash as a class: `npx tsc`, `node_modules/.bin/tsc`, and `pnpm run check` are three different binaries and entrypoints, all refused identically. serena's `get_diagnostics_for_file` is the right tool and the capability exists in the system, but the call wasn't permission-granted through my interface. No permissions allowlist exists in `.claude/settings.json`, so there's no in-repo edit that widens this. One surface is honestly recorded as **untested rather than exhausted**: subagents holding Bash, which an explicit session instruction forbids me from invoking — that's the first thing to re-test if you want execution proof.

**The fix** (`server/services/organizational-memory.ts`, lines 216 and 573). Both errors were the same anti-pattern:

```ts
const rawAdvice = (govResult as unknown as Record<string, unknown>).choices?.[0]?.message?.content;
```

`governedGenerate` returns `GovernedGenerateResult`, which has no `choices[]` envelope — that's the OpenAI wire shape, exposed here only as the optional `rawResult`. The cast made `.choices` `unknown`; optional chaining narrows `unknown` to `{}`, and indexing `{}` with `0` is TS7053 under `strict`. This was a live bug, not just bad typing: the expression was `undefined` at runtime, so both functions always took their fallback path.

Both now read the field the type declares, `content: string` (the post-governance text):
- `generatePreventionAdvice` → `govResult.content || 'Unable to generate advice.'`; the redundant `return advice as string` became `return advice`.
- `evaluatePersonaAlignment` → `const result: PersonaEvaluation = JSON.parse(govResult.content || '{}')`, against a new module-local interface mirroring the `persona_evaluation` json_schema declared just above it. `JSON.parse` returns `any`, so that's a plain assignment, not a cast.

No suppression directive, no `any` cast, no deleted code.

**Static verification, and its one real limit.** I read `GovernedGenerateResult` to confirm `content: string`; confirmed `strict: true` with `exactOptionalPropertyTypes` off, which makes `lastAlignmentScore: number | undefined` valid against drizzle's optional update-set mapped type; confirmed that column is numeric (not drizzle's string-typed `numeric`) because the already-compiling `getPersonaAlignment` maps it into a declared `number | null` — that was the one place the old `any` could have masked a mismatch. Changes are confined to one file, both exported signatures are unchanged, and `PersonaEvaluation` isn't exported, so nothing downstream shifts. The limit worth naming: static reasoning can't prove the absence of new errors in files I didn't read, which is exactly what executing `tsc` would have covered.

Two files I added that aren't product code, both at hooks' explicit instruction — say the word and I'll remove either: `build-os/packets/routing/routing-request.json` and `build-os/motion/exhaustion/current.json`.
